findings.claim: combined_figures marks a figure or monthly cell as resting on an override only when an overridden line is still in its evidence ({m.id for m in metrics_ if lines & set(m.evidence)}), while per-account case_figures also compares with the no-override figures (_rests_on, overrides.py:345-347, 389-395). An override that moves a line out of a figure changes that combined figure's value but leaves it unmarked in the workspace's 'All accounts' section, so the underwriter sees a changed trading-receipts figure with no 'rests on an override' flag (R17 broken on the new combined view).
findings.repro: Setup of tests/test_multi_account.py::test_override_marks_combined_figures: case main=MAIN, savings=SAVINGS; overrides.add_override(folder, 'S2', 'other', reason='not trading', name='Pat', account='savings'); both = overrides.combined_figures(overrides.case_figures(folder)). Combined M2 is 610.00, down from 660.00, but 'M2' not in both.marked and ('2026-01','trading_receipts') not in both.marked_cells, whereas 'M2' in overrides.case_figures(folder)['savings'].marked. The existing test asserts only M25.

findings.claim: An existing account whose statement cannot be read is skipped by the combined limit check, and an account whose statements/<key>.csv is missing is silently dropped by case_figures (overrides._load returns None, then continue), so the 'All accounts' section, captioned 'Across every account of the case' (COMBINED_BASIS), omits that account without saying so.
findings.repro: Three-account case main/savings/third; delete statements/third.csv; open the workspace: the 'All accounts' section shows figures over main and savings only, with no note that third is missing; with a third file that load_csv refuses, a fourth import is checked against the limit without third's amounts.
